v: A great sign appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet and a crown of twelve stars on her head.[^1]
Καὶ σημεῖον μέγα ὤφθη ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, γυνὴ περιβεβλημένη τὸν ἥλιον, καὶ ἡ σελήνη ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν αὐτῆς, καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτῆς στέφανος ἀστέρων δώδεκα,
She was pregnant, and she cried out in labor, in agony to give birth.[^2]
καὶ ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα· καὶ κράζει ὠδίνουσα καὶ βασανιζομένη τεκεῖν.
Then another sign appeared in heaven: there was a great red dragon,[^3] with seven heads and ten horns,[^4] and seven diadems[^5] on his heads.
καὶ ὤφθη ἄλλο σημεῖον ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, καὶ ἰδοὺ δράκων μέγας πυρρός, ἔχων κεφαλὰς ἑπτὰ καὶ κέρατα δέκα καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτοῦ ἑπτὰ διαδήματα,

His tail swept away a third of the stars of heaven and threw them to the earth.[^6] The dragon stood before the woman who was about to give birth, so that he might devour her child as soon as she gave birth.
καὶ ἡ οὐρὰ αὐτοῦ σύρει τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀστέρων τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἔβαλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν γῆν. καὶ ὁ δράκων ἕστηκεν ἐνώπιον τῆς γυναικὸς τῆς μελλούσης τεκεῖν, ἵνα ὅταν τέκῃ τὸ τέκνον αὐτῆς καταφάγῃ.
She gave birth to a son, a male child, who is going to rule all the nations with an iron rod.[^7] But her child was snatched up to God and to his throne.
καὶ ἔτεκεν υἱόν, ἄρσεν, ὃς μέλλει ποιμαίνειν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ἐν ῥάβδῳ σιδηρᾷ· καὶ ἡρπάσθη τὸ τέκνον αὐτῆς πρὸς τὸν θεὸν καὶ πρὸς τὸν θρόνον αὐτοῦ.
The woman fled into the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God, so that she might be taken care of there for 1,260 days.[^8]
καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἔφυγεν εἰς τὴν ἔρημον, ὅπου ἔχει ἐκεῖ τόπον ἡτοιμασμένον ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, ἵνα ἐκεῖ τρέφωσιν αὐτὴν ἡμέρας χιλίας διακοσίας ἑξήκοντα.
Then war broke out in heaven. Michael[^9] and his angels fought against the dragon. The dragon and his angels fought back,
Καὶ ἐγένετο πόλεμος ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, ὁ Μιχαὴλ καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτοῦ τοῦ πολεμῆσαι μετὰ τοῦ δράκοντος. καὶ ὁ δράκων ἐπολέμησεν καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτοῦ,
but he was not strong enough, and there was no longer any place for them in heaven.
καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσεν, οὐδὲ τόπος εὑρέθη αὐτῶν ἔτι ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ.

The great dragon was thrown down, that ancient serpent,[^10] who is called the devil and Satan,[^11] who deceives the whole world. He was thrown down to the earth, and his angels were thrown down with him.
καὶ ἐβλήθη ὁ δράκων ὁ μέγας, ὁ ὄφις ὁ ἀρχαῖος, ὁ καλούμενος Διάβολος καὶ ὁ Σατανᾶς, ὁ πλανῶν τὴν οἰκουμένην ὅλην— ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν γῆν, καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτοῦ μετʼ αὐτοῦ ἐβλήθησαν.

Then I heard a loud voice in heaven saying, "Now the salvation and the power and the kingdom of our God, and the authority of his Messiah,[^12] have come, for the accuser[^13] of our brothers and sisters[^14] has been thrown down, who accuses them before our God day and night.

Καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν μεγάλην ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ λέγουσαν· Ἄρτι ἐγένετο ἡ σωτηρία καὶ ἡ δύναμις καὶ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν καὶ ἡ ἐξουσία τοῦ χριστοῦ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἐβλήθη ὁ κατήγωρ τῶν ἀδελφῶν ἡμῶν, ὁ κατηγορῶν αὐτοὺς ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός.
They have conquered him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony, for they did not love their lives even in the face of death.[^15]
καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐνίκησαν αὐτὸν διὰ τὸ αἷμα τοῦ ἀρνίου καὶ διὰ τὸν λόγον τῆς μαρτυρίας αὐτῶν, καὶ οὐκ ἠγάπησαν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτῶν ἄχρι θανάτου·
So rejoice, you heavens, and you who dwell in them![^16] But woe[^17] to the earth and the sea, for the devil has come down to you in great fury, because he knows that his time is short."
διὰ τοῦτο εὐφραίνεσθε, οἱ οὐρανοὶ καὶ οἱ ἐν αὐτοῖς σκηνοῦντες. οὐαὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν, ὅτι κατέβη ὁ διάβολος πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἔχων θυμὸν μέγαν, εἰδὼς ὅτι ὀλίγον καιρὸν ἔχει.
When the dragon saw that he had been thrown down to the earth, he pursued the woman who had given birth to the male child.
Καὶ ὅτε εἶδεν ὁ δράκων ὅτι ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν γῆν, ἐδίωξεν τὴν γυναῖκα ἥτις ἔτεκεν τὸν ἄρσενα.

But the woman was given the two wings of the great eagle,[^18] so that she could fly into the wilderness, to her place, where she is taken care of for a time, times and half a time,[^19] away from the serpent.[^20]
καὶ ἐδόθησαν τῇ γυναικὶ αἱ δύο πτέρυγες τοῦ ἀετοῦ τοῦ μεγάλου, ἵνα πέτηται εἰς τὴν ἔρημον εἰς τὸν τόπον αὐτῆς, ὅπου τρέφεται ἐκεῖ καιρὸν καὶ καιροὺς καὶ ἥμισυ καιροῦ ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ ὄφεως.
Then the serpent poured water like a river out of his mouth after the woman, to sweep her away with the flood.
καὶ ἔβαλεν ὁ ὄφις ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ ὀπίσω τῆς γυναικὸς ὕδωρ ὡς ποταμόν, ἵνα αὐτὴν ποταμοφόρητον ποιήσῃ.
But the earth helped the woman. The earth opened its mouth and swallowed the river that the dragon had poured out of his mouth.[^21]
καὶ ἐβοήθησεν ἡ γῆ τῇ γυναικί, καὶ ἤνοιξεν ἡ γῆ τὸ στόμα αὐτῆς καὶ κατέπιεν τὸν ποταμὸν ὃν ἔβαλεν ὁ δράκων ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ·
Then the dragon was enraged with the woman, and went off to make war on the rest of her offspring,[^22] those who keep the commands of God and hold to the testimony of Jesus.
καὶ ὠργίσθη ὁ δράκων ἐπὶ τῇ γυναικί, καὶ ἀπῆλθεν ποιῆσαι πόλεμον μετὰ τῶν λοιπῶν τοῦ σπέρματος αὐτῆς, τῶν τηρούντων τὰς ἐντολὰς τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἐχόντων τὴν μαρτυρίαν Ἰησοῦ·
And he stood on the sand of the seashore.[^23]
καὶ ἐστάθη ἐπὶ τὴν ἄμμον τῆς θαλάσσης.

n.1: Compare Joseph's dream in Genesis 37:9, "The sun, the moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me."
n.2: Compare Isaiah 66:7–8; Micah 4:10.
n.3: Greek *drakon*, "dragon, serpent", used in the Greek Old Testament for monsters of the sea such as Leviathan (Isaiah 27:1, "he will kill the dragon that is in the sea"; Psalm 74:13–14). See verse 9.
n.4: Compare the fourth beast of Daniel 7:7, which "had ten horns".
n.5: Greek *diadema*, a royal crown, as distinct from a victor's wreath (*stephanos*, verse 1).
n.6: Compare Daniel 8:10, "it threw down to the earth some of the host and some of the stars".
n.7: Psalm 2:9; see the note on 2:27. Compare also Isaiah 66:7, "she delivered a son".
n.8: See the note on 11:2.
n.9: One of the chief angels, the guardian of Israel (Daniel 10:13, 21; 12:1; Jude 9).
n.10: The serpent of Genesis 3:1–15.
n.11: *Devil*: Greek *diabolos*, "slanderer". *Satan*: from the Hebrew *satan*, "adversary, accuser" (compare Job 1:6–12; Zechariah 3:1–2).
n.13: Greek *kategor*, an unusual form of *kategoros*, "accuser", the meaning of the Hebrew *satan*.
n.14: Greek *adelphoi*, "brothers", used of the believers, men and women alike.
n.15: Literally "they did not love their life until death".
n.16: Compare Isaiah 44:23; 49:13, "Shout for joy, you heavens!" *Dwell*: Greek *skenoo*, "live in a tent, dwell" (see 7:15).
n.18: Compare Exodus 19:4, "how I carried you on eagles' wings and brought you to myself"; Deuteronomy 32:11; Isaiah 40:31.
n.19: That is, probably three and a half years, as in Daniel 7:25; 12:7. See the note on 11:2.
n.20: Literally "from the face of the serpent".
n.21: Compare Exodus 15:12, "the earth swallowed them"; Numbers 16:30–32.
n.22: Literally "seed". Compare Genesis 3:15, "between your offspring and her offspring".
n.23: Many manuscripts read "And I stood on the sand of the seashore." In some English Bibles, including the King James Version, this sentence begins 13:1.

v: Then I saw a beast coming up out of the sea.[^1] It had ten horns and seven heads, with ten diadems on its horns, and blasphemous names[^2] on its heads.
Καὶ εἶδον ἐκ τῆς θαλάσσης θηρίον ἀναβαῖνον, ἔχον κέρατα δέκα καὶ κεφαλὰς ἑπτά, καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν κεράτων αὐτοῦ δέκα διαδήματα, καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτοῦ ὀνόματα βλασφημίας.
The beast that I saw was like a leopard. Its feet were like a bear's, and its mouth was like a lion's mouth.[^3] And the dragon gave it his power and his throne and great authority.
καὶ τὸ θηρίον ὃ εἶδον ἦν ὅμοιον παρδάλει, καὶ οἱ πόδες αὐτοῦ ὡς ἄρκου, καὶ τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ ὡς στόμα λέοντος. καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ ὁ δράκων τὴν δύναμιν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸν θρόνον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐξουσίαν μεγάλην.
One of its heads seemed to have been slaughtered to death,[^4] but its mortal wound had been healed. The whole earth was amazed and followed the beast.[^5]
καὶ μίαν ἐκ τῶν κεφαλῶν αὐτοῦ ὡς ἐσφαγμένην εἰς θάνατον, καὶ ἡ πληγὴ τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ ἐθεραπεύθη. καὶ ἐθαυμάσθη ὅλη ἡ γῆ ὀπίσω τοῦ θηρίου,
They worshiped the dragon, because he had given his authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast, saying, "Who is like the beast,[^6] and who can make war against it?"
καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ δράκοντι ὅτι ἔδωκεν τὴν ἐξουσίαν τῷ θηρίῳ, καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ θηρίῳ λέγοντες· Τίς ὅμοιος τῷ θηρίῳ, καὶ τίς δύναται πολεμῆσαι μετʼ αὐτοῦ;
The beast was given a mouth speaking arrogant words and blasphemies,[^7] and it was allowed to exercise authority[^8] for forty-two months.[^9]
Καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ στόμα λαλοῦν μεγάλα καὶ βλασφημίας, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ἐξουσία ποιῆσαι μῆνας τεσσεράκοντα δύο.
It opened its mouth to utter blasphemies against God, blaspheming his name and his dwelling,[^10] that is, those who dwell in heaven.
καὶ ἤνοιξε τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ εἰς βλασφημίας πρὸς τὸν θεόν, βλασφημῆσαι τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν σκηνὴν αὐτοῦ, τοὺς ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ σκηνοῦντας.
It was allowed to make war on God's holy people[^11] and to conquer them.[^12] And it was given authority over every tribe and people and language and nation.
καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ποιῆσαι πόλεμον μετὰ τῶν ἁγίων καὶ νικῆσαι αὐτούς, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ἐξουσία ἐπὶ πᾶσαν φυλὴν καὶ λαὸν καὶ γλῶσσαν καὶ ἔθνος.
All who live on the earth will worship it, everyone whose name has not been written, since the foundation of the world, in the book of life of the Lamb who was slaughtered.[^13]
καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν αὐτὸν πάντες οἱ κατοικοῦντες ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, οὗ οὐ γέγραπται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τῆς ζωῆς τοῦ ἀρνίου τοῦ ἐσφαγμένου ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου.
If anyone has ears, let them hear.
Εἴ τις ἔχει οὖς ἀκουσάτω.

If anyone is to go into captivity, into captivity they will go.[^14] If anyone is to be killed with the sword, with the sword they will be killed.[^15] This calls for the endurance and the faithfulness of God's holy people.[^16]
εἴ τις εἰς αἰχμαλωσίαν, εἰς αἰχμαλωσίαν ὑπάγει· εἴ τις ἐν μαχαίρῃ ἀποκτανθῆναι αὐτὸν ἐν μαχαίρῃ ἀποκτανθῆναι. ὧδέ ἐστιν ἡ ὑπομονὴ καὶ ἡ πίστις τῶν ἁγίων.
Then I saw another beast coming up out of the earth. It had two horns like a lamb, and it spoke like a dragon.
Καὶ εἶδον ἄλλο θηρίον ἀναβαῖνον ἐκ τῆς γῆς, καὶ εἶχεν κέρατα δύο ὅμοια ἀρνίῳ, καὶ ἐλάλει ὡς δράκων.
It exercised all the authority of the first beast on its behalf,[^17] and it made the earth and those who live on it worship the first beast, whose mortal wound had been healed.
καὶ τὴν ἐξουσίαν τοῦ πρώτου θηρίου πᾶσαν ποιεῖ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ. καὶ ποιεῖ τὴν γῆν καὶ τοὺς ἐν αὐτῇ κατοικοῦντας ἵνα προσκυνήσουσιν τὸ θηρίον τὸ πρῶτον, οὗ ἐθεραπεύθη ἡ πληγὴ τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ.
It performed great signs, even making fire come down from heaven to earth in front of people.[^18]
καὶ ποιεῖ σημεῖα μεγάλα, ἵνα καὶ πῦρ ποιῇ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβαίνειν εἰς τὴν γῆν ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων.

And it deceived those who live on the earth[^19] by the signs that it was allowed to perform on behalf of the beast, telling those who live on the earth to make an image for the beast that had been wounded by the sword and yet lived.[^20]
καὶ πλανᾷ τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς διὰ τὰ σημεῖα ἃ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ποιῆσαι ἐνώπιον τοῦ θηρίου, λέγων τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ποιῆσαι εἰκόνα τῷ θηρίῳ, ὃς ἔχει τὴν πληγὴν τῆς μαχαίρης καὶ ἔζησεν.
It was allowed to give breath[^21] to the image of the beast, so that the image of the beast could even speak, and could cause all who would not worship the image of the beast to be killed.[^22]
καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ δοῦναι πνεῦμα τῇ εἰκόνι τοῦ θηρίου, ἵνα καὶ λαλήσῃ ἡ εἰκὼν τοῦ θηρίου καὶ ποιήσῃ ἵνα ὅσοι ἐὰν μὴ προσκυνήσωσιν τῇ εἰκόνι τοῦ θηρίου ἀποκτανθῶσιν.
It also made everyone, small and great, rich and poor, free and slave, receive a mark on their right hand or on their forehead,[^23]

καὶ ποιεῖ πάντας, τοὺς μικροὺς καὶ τοὺς μεγάλους, καὶ τοὺς πλουσίους καὶ τοὺς πτωχούς, καὶ τοὺς ἐλευθέρους καὶ τοὺς δούλους, ἵνα δῶσιν αὐτοῖς χάραγμα ἐπὶ τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῶν τῆς δεξιᾶς ἢ ἐπὶ τὸ μέτωπον αὐτῶν,
so that no one could buy or sell unless they had the mark, that is, the name of the beast or the number of its name.
καὶ ἵνα μή τις δύνηται ἀγοράσαι ἢ πωλῆσαι εἰ μὴ ὁ ἔχων τὸ χάραγμα, τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ θηρίου ἢ τὸν ἀριθμὸν τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ.
This calls for wisdom.[^24] Let the one who has understanding calculate the number of the beast, for it is the number of a human being.[^25] Its number is 666.[^26]
ὧδε ἡ σοφία ἐστίν· ὁ ἔχων νοῦν ψηφισάτω τὸν ἀριθμὸν τοῦ θηρίου, ἀριθμὸς γὰρ ἀνθρώπου ἐστίν· καὶ ὁ ἀριθμὸς αὐτοῦ ἑξακόσιοι ἑξήκοντα ἕξ.

n.1: Compare Daniel 7:3, "Four great beasts came up out of the sea". The beast of this chapter combines features of all four of Daniel's beasts (Daniel 7:4–7; compare verse 2).
n.2: Some editions read "a blasphemous name".
n.3: Compare Daniel 7:4–6: the lion, the bear and the leopard.
n.4: Literally "as slaughtered to death", the same word as that used of the Lamb in 5:6; also in verse 8. *Mortal wound*: literally "the wound of its death"; also in verse 12.
n.5: Literally "marveled after the beast".
n.6: A parody of the praise of God in Exodus 15:11, "Who is like you among the gods, LORD?"; compare Psalm 35:10.
n.7: Compare Daniel 7:8, 20, "a mouth speaking arrogant words", and 11:36.
n.8: Literally "it was given authority to act". Many manuscripts read "authority to make war".
n.9: See the note on 11:2.
n.10: Greek *skene*, "tent, tabernacle", from the same root as "dwell" (*skenoo*) later in the verse.
n.11: Literally "the holy ones", traditionally "the saints"; also in verse 10.
n.12: Compare Daniel 7:21, "this horn was making war against the holy ones and was prevailing over them".
n.13: Or "in the book of life of the Lamb who was slaughtered from the foundation of the world". The Greek may be read either way; compare 17:8.
n.14: Compare Jeremiah 15:2, "those destined for the sword, to the sword; … and those destined for captivity, to captivity"; 43:11. Many manuscripts read "If anyone holds captives, they go away".
n.15: The SBLGNT here follows NA28; other editions read "If anyone kills with the sword, with the sword they must be killed."
n.16: Literally "Here is the endurance and the faith of the holy ones".
n.17: Literally "before it", "in its presence"; also in verse 14.
n.18: Compare 1 Kings 18:38, "Then the fire of the LORD fell"; 2 Kings 1:10.
n.19: Many manuscripts read "it deceived my own people who live on the earth".
n.20: Compare Daniel 3:1–7, where all are commanded to worship Nebuchadnezzar's statue of gold, in the Greek Old Testament his *eikon*, "image".
n.22: Compare Daniel 3:5–6, "Whoever does not fall down and worship will immediately be thrown into a furnace of blazing fire."
n.23: Greek *charagma*, "mark, stamp, brand", a word used of the image or seal stamped on coins and documents; also in verse 17.
n.25: Or "a human number", "the number of a man".
n.26: Greek *hexakosioi hexekonta hex*, "six hundred sixty-six", written out in words, as in the SBLGNT and most editions; Tregelles prints it with Greek letters used as numerals (χξϛ). The apparatus records no other number. In Greek and Hebrew, letters also served as numbers, so that every name had a numerical value, the practice later called gematria. Interpreters have proposed many names whose letters add up to 666; one often suggested is "Nero Caesar" written in Hebrew letters (*nrwn qsr*). The text does not say whose name is meant.

v: Then I looked, and there was the Lamb, standing on Mount Zion,[^1] and with him 144,000 who had his name and his Father's name written on their foreheads.
Καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ τὸ ἀρνίον ἑστὸς ἐπὶ τὸ ὄρος Σιών, καὶ μετʼ αὐτοῦ ἑκατὸν τεσσεράκοντα τέσσαρες χιλιάδες ἔχουσαι τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ γεγραμμένον ἐπὶ τῶν μετώπων αὐτῶν.
And I heard a sound from heaven like the sound of many waters and like the sound of loud thunder. The sound I heard was like harpists playing on their harps.
καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ὡς φωνὴν ὑδάτων πολλῶν καὶ ὡς φωνὴν βροντῆς μεγάλης, καὶ ἡ φωνὴ ἣν ἤκουσα ὡς κιθαρῳδῶν κιθαριζόντων ἐν ταῖς κιθάραις αὐτῶν.
They sang what seemed to be a new song[^2] before the throne and before the four living creatures and the elders. No one could learn the song except the 144,000 who had been bought from the earth.

καὶ ᾄδουσιν ὡς ᾠδὴν καινὴν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου καὶ ἐνώπιον τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων· καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο μαθεῖν τὴν ᾠδὴν εἰ μὴ αἱ ἑκατὸν τεσσεράκοντα τέσσαρες χιλιάδες, οἱ ἠγορασμένοι ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς.

These are the ones who have not defiled themselves with women, for they are virgins.[^3] These are the ones who follow the Lamb wherever he goes. They have been bought[^4] from among humankind as firstfruits[^5] for God and for the Lamb,
οὗτοί εἰσιν οἳ μετὰ γυναικῶν οὐκ ἐμολύνθησαν, παρθένοι γάρ εἰσιν· οὗτοι οἱ ἀκολουθοῦντες τῷ ἀρνίῳ ὅπου ἂν ὑπάγῃ· οὗτοι ἠγοράσθησαν ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀπαρχὴ τῷ θεῷ καὶ τῷ ἀρνίῳ,
and no lie was found in their mouths;[^6] they are blameless.
καὶ ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτῶν οὐχ εὑρέθη ψεῦδος· ἄμωμοί εἰσιν.
Then I saw another angel flying in midheaven, with eternal good news to proclaim to those who live[^7] on the earth, to every nation and tribe and language and people.
Καὶ εἶδον ἄλλον ἄγγελον πετόμενον ἐν μεσουρανήματι, ἔχοντα εὐαγγέλιον αἰώνιον εὐαγγελίσαι ἐπὶ τοὺς καθημένους ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ἐπὶ πᾶν ἔθνος καὶ φυλὴν καὶ γλῶσσαν καὶ λαόν,
He said with a loud voice, "Fear God[^8] and give him glory, for the hour of his judgment has come. Worship him who made heaven and earth, the sea and the springs of water."[^9]
λέγων ἐν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ· Φοβήθητε τὸν θεὸν καὶ δότε αὐτῷ δόξαν, ὅτι ἦλθεν ἡ ὥρα τῆς κρίσεως αὐτοῦ, καὶ προσκυνήσατε τῷ ποιήσαντι τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ θάλασσαν καὶ πηγὰς ὑδάτων.
Another angel, a second, followed, saying, "Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great,[^10] who made all the nations drink the wine of the passion of her sexual immorality!"[^11]
Καὶ ἄλλος δεύτερος ἄγγελος ἠκολούθησεν λέγων· Ἔπεσεν, ἔπεσεν Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη, ἣ ἐκ τοῦ οἴνου τοῦ θυμοῦ τῆς πορνείας αὐτῆς πεπότικεν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη.
Another angel, a third, followed them, saying with a loud voice, "If anyone worships the beast and its image, and receives a mark on their forehead or on their hand,
Καὶ ἄλλος ἄγγελος τρίτος ἠκολούθησεν αὐτοῖς λέγων ἐν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ· Εἴ τις προσκυνεῖ τὸ θηρίον καὶ τὴν εἰκόνα αὐτοῦ, καὶ λαμβάνει χάραγμα ἐπὶ τοῦ μετώπου αὐτοῦ ἢ ἐπὶ τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ,

they too will drink the wine of God's fury, poured out undiluted[^12] into the cup of his anger.[^13] They will be tormented with fire and sulfur in the presence of the holy angels and in the presence of the Lamb.[^14]
καὶ αὐτὸς πίεται ἐκ τοῦ οἴνου τοῦ θυμοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ κεκερασμένου ἀκράτου ἐν τῷ ποτηρίῳ τῆς ὀργῆς αὐτοῦ, καὶ βασανισθήσεται ἐν πυρὶ καὶ θείῳ ἐνώπιον ἀγγέλων ἁγίων καὶ ἐνώπιον τοῦ ἀρνίου.
The smoke of their torment goes up forever and ever.[^15] There is no rest day or night for those who worship the beast and its image, and for anyone who receives the mark of its name."

καὶ ὁ καπνὸς τοῦ βασανισμοῦ αὐτῶν εἰς αἰῶνας αἰώνων ἀναβαίνει, καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσιν ἀνάπαυσιν ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός, οἱ προσκυνοῦντες τὸ θηρίον καὶ τὴν εἰκόνα αὐτοῦ, καὶ εἴ τις λαμβάνει τὸ χάραγμα τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ.
This calls for the endurance of God's holy people,[^16] those who keep the commands of God and their faith in Jesus.[^17]
Ὧδε ἡ ὑπομονὴ τῶν ἁγίων ἐστίν, οἱ τηροῦντες τὰς ἐντολὰς τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τὴν πίστιν Ἰησοῦ.
Then I heard a voice from heaven saying, "Write: Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on." "Yes," says the Spirit, "they will rest from their labors, for their works go with them."[^18]

Καὶ ἤκουσα φωνῆς ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ λεγούσης· Γράψον· Μακάριοι οἱ νεκροὶ οἱ ἐν κυρίῳ ἀποθνῄσκοντες ἀπʼ ἄρτι. ναί, λέγει τὸ πνεῦμα, ἵνα ἀναπαήσονται ἐκ τῶν κόπων αὐτῶν, τὰ γὰρ ἔργα αὐτῶν ἀκολουθεῖ μετʼ αὐτῶν.
Then I looked, and there was a white cloud, and seated on the cloud was one like a son of man,[^19] with a golden crown on his head and a sharp sickle in his hand.
Καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ νεφέλη λευκή, καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν νεφέλην καθήμενον ὅμοιον υἱὸν ἀνθρώπου, ἔχων ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ στέφανον χρυσοῦν καὶ ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ δρέπανον ὀξύ.

Another angel came out of the temple, calling with a loud voice to the one seated on the cloud, "Put in your sickle and reap, for the hour to reap has come, because the harvest of the earth is ripe."[^20]
καὶ ἄλλος ἄγγελος ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ τοῦ ναοῦ κράζων ἐν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπὶ τῆς νεφέλης· Πέμψον τὸ δρέπανόν σου καὶ θέρισον, ὅτι ἦλθεν ἡ ὥρα θερίσαι, ὅτι ἐξηράνθη ὁ θερισμὸς τῆς γῆς.
So the one seated on the cloud swung his sickle over the earth, and the earth was harvested.
καὶ ἔβαλεν ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τῆς νεφέλης τὸ δρέπανον αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν, καὶ ἐθερίσθη ἡ γῆ.
Another angel came out of the temple in heaven, and he too had a sharp sickle.
Καὶ ἄλλος ἄγγελος ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ τοῦ ναοῦ τοῦ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, ἔχων καὶ αὐτὸς δρέπανον ὀξύ.

Then another angel came from the altar,[^21] the one who has authority over fire, and he called with a loud voice to the one who had the sharp sickle, "Put in your sharp sickle and gather the clusters from the vine of the earth, for its grapes are ripe."

καὶ ἄλλος ἄγγελος ἐκ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου, ὁ ἔχων ἐξουσίαν ἐπὶ τοῦ πυρός, καὶ ἐφώνησεν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ τῷ ἔχοντι τὸ δρέπανον τὸ ὀξὺ λέγων· Πέμψον σου τὸ δρέπανον τὸ ὀξὺ καὶ τρύγησον τοὺς βότρυας τῆς ἀμπέλου τῆς γῆς, ὅτι ἤκμασαν αἱ σταφυλαὶ αὐτῆς.
So the angel swung his sickle over the earth and gathered the vintage of the earth, and he threw it into the great winepress of God's fury.[^22]
καὶ ἔβαλεν ὁ ἄγγελος τὸ δρέπανον αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν γῆν, καὶ ἐτρύγησεν τὴν ἄμπελον τῆς γῆς, καὶ ἔβαλεν εἰς τὴν ληνὸν τοῦ θυμοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ τὸν μέγαν.
The winepress was trodden outside the city, and blood flowed from the winepress as high as the horses' bridles, for a distance of 1,600 stadia.[^23]
καὶ ἐπατήθη ἡ ληνὸς ἔξωθεν τῆς πόλεως, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν αἷμα ἐκ τῆς ληνοῦ ἄχρι τῶν χαλινῶν τῶν ἵππων ἀπὸ σταδίων χιλίων ἑξακοσίων.

n.1: Compare Psalm 2:6, "I myself have installed my king on Zion, my holy mountain"; Joel 3:5 (2:32 in most English Bibles).
n.2: Many manuscripts read "They sang a new song".
n.3: Greek *parthenoi*, "virgins", here used of men. The image may draw on the rule that Israel's soldiers kept away from women while on campaign (1 Samuel 21:5–6; 21:4–5 in most English Bibles; 2 Samuel 11:11), or on the prophets' picture of idolatry as sexual unfaithfulness (compare 2:14, 20).
n.4: Many manuscripts add "by Jesus".
n.5: The first and best part of the harvest, which belonged to God (Exodus 23:19; compare Jeremiah 2:3).
n.6: Compare Zephaniah 3:13, "and no deceitful tongue will be found in their mouths"; Isaiah 53:9.
n.7: Literally "those who sit", that is, are settled.
n.8: Many manuscripts read "Fear the Lord".
n.9: Compare Exodus 20:11, "For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, the sea and everything in them"; Psalm 146:6.
n.10: Isaiah 21:9, "Fallen, fallen is Babylon!"; compare Jeremiah 51:7–8 and Daniel 4:27 (4:30 in most English Bibles), "Is this not great Babylon". Many manuscripts have "Fallen" only once.
n.11: Greek *thymos* means both "passion" and "fury", as in "God's fury" in verse 10. Compare Jeremiah 51:7, "The nations drank her wine; therefore the nations have gone mad."
n.12: Literally "mixed undiluted". Wine was normally mixed with water.
n.13: Compare Psalm 75:9 (75:8 in most English Bibles), "For in the hand of the LORD there is a cup, with foaming wine"; Isaiah 51:17; Jeremiah 25:15.
n.15: Isaiah 34:10, "its smoke will go up forever".
n.16: Literally "Here is the endurance of the holy ones", traditionally "the saints".
n.17: Or "and the faith of Jesus", "faithfulness to Jesus".
n.18: Or "Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord. From now on, yes, says the Spirit, they will rest …". *Go with them*: literally "follow with them".
n.19: That is, one in human form. See 1:13; Daniel 7:13.
n.20: Joel 4:13 (3:13 in most English Bibles), "Swing the sickle, for the harvest is ripe". *Is ripe*: literally "has dried", that is, is fully ripe.
n.21: Literally "And another angel from the altar". The SBLGNT here follows the margin of Westcott and Hort; the other editions read "came out from the altar".
n.22: Compare Isaiah 63:3, "I have trodden the winepress alone"; Lamentations 1:15; Joel 4:13 (3:13 in most English Bibles), "Come, tread the grapes, for the winepress is full."
n.23: About 180 miles (300 kilometers). A *stadion* was about 600 feet (185 meters).

v: Then I saw another sign in heaven, great and amazing: seven angels with seven plagues, which are the last, for with them the fury of God is completed.
Καὶ εἶδον ἄλλο σημεῖον ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ μέγα καὶ θαυμαστόν, ἀγγέλους ἑπτὰ ἔχοντας πληγὰς ἑπτὰ τὰς ἐσχάτας, ὅτι ἐν αὐταῖς ἐτελέσθη ὁ θυμὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.

And I saw what looked like a sea of glass mixed with fire, and those who had conquered the beast and its image and the number of its name, standing on the sea of glass[^1] and holding harps of God.[^2]

Καὶ εἶδον ὡς θάλασσαν ὑαλίνην μεμιγμένην πυρί, καὶ τοὺς νικῶντας ἐκ τοῦ θηρίου καὶ ἐκ τῆς εἰκόνος αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκ τοῦ ἀριθμοῦ τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ ἑστῶτας ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν τὴν ὑαλίνην, ἔχοντας κιθάρας τοῦ θεοῦ.
They sang the song of Moses, the servant of God,[^3] and the song of the Lamb: "Great and amazing are your works, Lord God Almighty![^4] Just and true are your ways, King of the ages![^5]

καὶ ᾄδουσιν τὴν ᾠδὴν Μωϋσέως τοῦ δούλου τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τὴν ᾠδὴν τοῦ ἀρνίου λέγοντες· Μεγάλα καὶ θαυμαστὰ τὰ ἔργα σου, κύριε, ὁ θεός, ὁ παντοκράτωρ· δίκαιαι καὶ ἀληθιναὶ αἱ ὁδοί σου, ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν αἰώνων·
Who will not fear you, Lord, and glorify your name? For you alone are holy. All the nations will come and worship before you,[^6] for your righteous acts[^7] have been revealed."
τίς οὐ μὴ φοβηθῇ, κύριε, καὶ δοξάσει τὸ ὄνομά σου, ὅτι μόνος ὅσιος; ὅτι πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ἥξουσιν καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν ἐνώπιόν σου, ὅτι τὰ δικαιώματά σου ἐφανερώθησαν.
After this I looked, and the temple of the tent of the testimony[^8] in heaven was opened,
Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα εἶδον, καὶ ἠνοίγη ὁ ναὸς τῆς σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ,
and out of the temple came the seven angels who had the seven plagues, dressed in clean, shining linen,[^9] with golden sashes around their chests.
καὶ ἐξῆλθον οἱ ἑπτὰ ἄγγελοι οἱ ἔχοντες τὰς ἑπτὰ πληγὰς ἐκ τοῦ ναοῦ, ἐνδεδυμένοι λίνον καθαρὸν λαμπρὸν καὶ περιεζωσμένοι περὶ τὰ στήθη ζώνας χρυσᾶς.
Then one of the four living creatures gave the seven angels seven golden bowls full of the fury of God, who lives forever and ever.
καὶ ἓν ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων ἔδωκεν τοῖς ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλοις ἑπτὰ φιάλας χρυσᾶς γεμούσας τοῦ θυμοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων.
The temple was filled with smoke from the glory of God and from his power,[^10] and no one could enter the temple until the seven plagues of the seven angels were completed.
καὶ ἐγεμίσθη ὁ ναὸς καπνοῦ ἐκ τῆς δόξης τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἐκ τῆς δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὸν ναὸν ἄχρι τελεσθῶσιν αἱ ἑπτὰ πληγαὶ τῶν ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλων.

n.1: Or "beside the sea of glass".
n.2: That is, harps for the worship of God, or given by God.
n.3: Compare the song Moses and the Israelites sang after crossing the sea (Exodus 15:1–18), and the song of Moses in Deuteronomy 32. The words of this song are drawn from many passages of the Old Testament.
n.4: Compare Psalm 111:2, "Great are the works of the LORD"; 139:14, "Wonderful are your works". *Almighty*: see 1:8.
n.5: Compare Deuteronomy 32:4, "all his ways are just"; Psalm 145:17. The SBLGNT here follows Westcott and Hort. Many manuscripts and most other editions read "King of the nations", as in Jeremiah 10:7.
n.6: Compare Jeremiah 10:7, "Who would not fear you, King of the nations?"; Psalm 86:9, "All the nations you have made will come and bow down before you, Lord, and they will glorify your name." In the Hebrew of Psalm 86:9, "Lord" is *Adonai*.
n.7: Or "your just decrees". Greek *dikaiomata*.
n.8: The tabernacle, called "the tabernacle of the testimony" in Exodus 38:21 and Numbers 1:50. *The testimony* was the stone tablets of the covenant kept in the ark (Exodus 25:16).
n.9: Some manuscripts read "dressed in clean, shining stone".
n.10: Compare Exodus 40:34–35, "the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle"; Isaiah 6:4, "and the house was filled with smoke"; 1 Kings 8:10–11.

v: Then I heard a loud voice from the temple saying to the seven angels, "Go and pour out on the earth the seven bowls of God's fury."
Καὶ ἤκουσα μεγάλης φωνῆς ἐκ τοῦ ναοῦ λεγούσης τοῖς ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλοις· Ὑπάγετε καὶ ἐκχέετε τὰς ἑπτὰ φιάλας τοῦ θυμοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς τὴν γῆν.
So the first angel went and poured out his bowl on the earth, and foul and painful sores[^1] broke out on the people who had the mark of the beast and who worshiped its image.
Καὶ ἀπῆλθεν ὁ πρῶτος καὶ ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν γῆν· καὶ ἐγένετο ἕλκος κακὸν καὶ πονηρὸν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τοὺς ἔχοντας τὸ χάραγμα τοῦ θηρίου καὶ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας τῇ εἰκόνι αὐτοῦ.
The second angel poured out his bowl into the sea, and it became blood like that of a corpse, and every living thing in the sea died.[^2]
Καὶ ὁ δεύτερος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν· καὶ ἐγένετο αἷμα ὡς νεκροῦ, καὶ πᾶσα ψυχὴ ζωῆς ἀπέθανεν τὰ ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ.
The third angel poured out his bowl into the rivers and the springs of water, and they became blood.
Καὶ ὁ τρίτος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ εἰς τοὺς ποταμοὺς καὶ τὰς πηγὰς τῶν ὑδάτων· καὶ ἐγένετο αἷμα.
And I heard the angel of the waters say, "You are just, Holy One, who is and who was,[^3] because you have judged these things.
καὶ ἤκουσα τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῶν ὑδάτων λέγοντος· Δίκαιος εἶ, ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν, ὁ ὅσιος, ὅτι ταῦτα ἔκρινας,
For they poured out the blood of God's holy people[^4] and of prophets, and you have given them blood to drink.[^5] They deserve it."[^6]
ὅτι αἷμα ἁγίων καὶ προφητῶν ἐξέχεαν, καὶ αἷμα αὐτοῖς δέδωκας πιεῖν· ἄξιοί εἰσιν.
And I heard the altar say, "Yes, Lord God Almighty, true and just are your judgments."[^7]
καὶ ἤκουσα τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου λέγοντος· Ναί, κύριε, ὁ θεός, ὁ παντοκράτωρ, ἀληθιναὶ καὶ δίκαιαι αἱ κρίσεις σου.
The fourth angel poured out his bowl on the sun, and it was allowed to scorch people with fire.
Καὶ ὁ τέταρτος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν ἥλιον· καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ καυματίσαι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἐν πυρί.
People were scorched by the fierce heat, and they blasphemed the name of God, who had authority over these plagues, and they did not repent and give him glory.
καὶ ἐκαυματίσθησαν οἱ ἄνθρωποι καῦμα μέγα· καὶ ἐβλασφήμησαν τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ἔχοντος τὴν ἐξουσίαν ἐπὶ τὰς πληγὰς ταύτας, καὶ οὐ μετενόησαν δοῦναι αὐτῷ δόξαν.
The fifth angel poured out his bowl on the throne of the beast, and its kingdom was plunged into darkness.[^8] People gnawed their tongues in agony,
Καὶ ὁ πέμπτος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν θρόνον τοῦ θηρίου· καὶ ἐγένετο ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ ἐσκοτωμένη, καὶ ἐμασῶντο τὰς γλώσσας αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ πόνου,
and they blasphemed the God of heaven because of their pains and their sores, and they did not repent of their works.
καὶ ἐβλασφήμησαν τὸν θεὸν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐκ τῶν πόνων αὐτῶν καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἑλκῶν αὐτῶν, καὶ οὐ μετενόησαν ἐκ τῶν ἔργων αὐτῶν.
The sixth angel poured out his bowl on the great river Euphrates, and its water was dried up,[^9] to prepare the way for the kings from the east.[^10]
Καὶ ὁ ἕκτος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν ποταμὸν τὸν μέγαν τὸν Εὐφράτην· καὶ ἐξηράνθη τὸ ὕδωρ αὐτοῦ, ἵνα ἑτοιμασθῇ ἡ ὁδὸς τῶν βασιλέων τῶν ἀπὸ ἀνατολῆς ἡλίου.
Then I saw three unclean spirits like frogs[^11] coming out of the mouth of the dragon, out of the mouth of the beast, and out of the mouth of the false prophet.[^12]
καὶ εἶδον ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦ δράκοντος καὶ ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦ θηρίου καὶ ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦ ψευδοπροφήτου πνεύματα τρία ἀκάθαρτα ὡς βάτραχοι·
For they are spirits of demons, performing signs, who go out to the kings of the whole world, to gather them for the battle on the great day of God Almighty.[^13]
εἰσὶν γὰρ πνεύματα δαιμονίων ποιοῦντα σημεῖα, ἃ ἐκπορεύεται ἐπὶ τοὺς βασιλεῖς τῆς οἰκουμένης ὅλης, συναγαγεῖν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν πόλεμον τῆς ἡμέρας τῆς μεγάλης τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ παντοκράτορος—
("Look, I am coming like a thief! Blessed is the one who stays awake and keeps their clothes on, so that they will not go about naked and be seen in their shame.")[^14]
Ἰδοὺ ἔρχομαι ὡς κλέπτης. μακάριος ὁ γρηγορῶν καὶ τηρῶν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ, ἵνα μὴ γυμνὸς περιπατῇ καὶ βλέπωσιν τὴν ἀσχημοσύνην αὐτοῦ—
And they gathered them at the place that is called in Hebrew Armageddon.[^15]
καὶ συνήγαγεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν τόπον τὸν καλούμενον Ἑβραϊστὶ Ἁρμαγεδών.
The seventh angel poured out his bowl into the air, and a loud voice came out of the temple,[^16] from the throne, saying, "It is done!"
Καὶ ὁ ἕβδομος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν ἀέρα— καὶ ἐξῆλθεν φωνὴ μεγάλη ἐκ τοῦ ναοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ θρόνου λέγουσα· Γέγονεν—

There were flashes of lightning, rumblings and peals of thunder, and there was a great earthquake, such as had never been since people have been on the earth,[^17] so mighty and so great was that earthquake.
καὶ ἐγένοντο ἀστραπαὶ καὶ φωναὶ καὶ βρονταί, καὶ σεισμὸς ἐγένετο μέγας, οἷος οὐκ ἐγένετο ἀφʼ οὗ ἄνθρωποι ἐγένοντο ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς τηλικοῦτος σεισμὸς οὕτω μέγας,
The great city was split into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell. God remembered Babylon the great[^18] and gave her the cup of the wine of the fury of his anger.
καὶ ἐγένετο ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη εἰς τρία μέρη, καὶ αἱ πόλεις τῶν ἐθνῶν ἔπεσαν· καὶ Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη ἐμνήσθη ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ δοῦναι αὐτῇ τὸ ποτήριον τοῦ οἴνου τοῦ θυμοῦ τῆς ὀργῆς αὐτοῦ·
Every island fled away, and the mountains could no longer be found.
καὶ πᾶσα νῆσος ἔφυγεν, καὶ ὄρη οὐχ εὑρέθησαν.
Huge hailstones, each weighing about a talent,[^19] fell from heaven on people, and people blasphemed God because of the plague of hail, for that plague was extremely severe.[^20]
καὶ χάλαζα μεγάλη ὡς ταλαντιαία καταβαίνει ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους· καὶ ἐβλασφήμησαν οἱ ἄνθρωποι τὸν θεὸν ἐκ τῆς πληγῆς τῆς χαλάζης, ὅτι μεγάλη ἐστὶν ἡ πληγὴ αὐτῆς σφόδρα.

n.1: Literally "a bad and evil sore". Compare the sixth plague of Egypt, Exodus 9:9–11, "boils that broke out into sores on people and animals".
n.2: Literally "every living soul, the things in the sea, died". Compare the first plague of Egypt, Exodus 7:17–21.
n.3: As in 11:17, the title lacks "who is to come".
n.4: Literally "of the holy ones", traditionally "of the saints".
n.5: Compare Isaiah 49:26, "they will be drunk on their own blood as on new wine".
n.6: Literally "They are worthy."
n.7: Compare Psalm 19:10 (19:9 in most English Bibles), "the rulings of the LORD are true, and righteous altogether"; 119:137. *Almighty*: see 1:8.
n.8: Literally "its kingdom became darkened". Compare the ninth plague of Egypt, Exodus 10:21–23.
n.9: Compare Isaiah 11:15; 44:27; Jeremiah 50:38, "A drought on her waters, and they will dry up!"; 51:36.
n.10: Literally "from the rising of the sun".
n.11: Compare the second plague of Egypt, Exodus 7:26–8:11 (8:1–15 in most English Bibles).
n.14: Compare 3:3, 18; Matthew 24:43; 1 Thessalonians 5:2. *Keeps their clothes on*: literally "keeps his garments".
n.15: Greek *Harmagedon*, probably from the Hebrew *har megiddo*, "the mountain of Megiddo". Megiddo, at the edge of the plain of Jezreel, was the site of famous battles (Judges 5:19; 2 Kings 23:29; compare Zechariah 12:11).
n.16: Many manuscripts read "the temple of heaven".
n.17: Compare Daniel 12:1, "a time of distress such as has never been since there was a nation".
n.18: Literally "Babylon the great was remembered before God". See 14:8.
n.19: Greek *talantiaios*, "weighing a talent", about 75 pounds (34 kilograms).
n.20: Compare the seventh plague of Egypt, Exodus 9:23–25.

v: Then one of the seven angels who had the seven bowls came and said to me,[^1] "Come, I will show you the judgment of the great prostitute, who is seated on many waters.[^2]
Καὶ ἦλθεν εἷς ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλων τῶν ἐχόντων τὰς ἑπτὰ φιάλας, καὶ ἐλάλησεν μετʼ ἐμοῦ λέγων· Δεῦρο, δείξω σοι τὸ κρίμα τῆς πόρνης τῆς μεγάλης τῆς καθημένης ἐπὶ ὑδάτων πολλῶν,
The kings of the earth committed sexual immorality with her, and those who live on the earth became drunk with the wine of her sexual immorality."[^3]
μεθʼ ἧς ἐπόρνευσαν οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς, καὶ ἐμεθύσθησαν οἱ κατοικοῦντες τὴν γῆν ἐκ τοῦ οἴνου τῆς πορνείας αὐτῆς.
Then he carried me away in the Spirit[^4] into a wilderness. There I saw a woman seated on a scarlet beast that was covered with blasphemous names, and it had seven heads and ten horns.
καὶ ἀπήνεγκέν με εἰς ἔρημον ἐν πνεύματι. καὶ εἶδον γυναῖκα καθημένην ἐπὶ θηρίον κόκκινον, γέμοντα ὀνόματα βλασφημίας, ἔχων κεφαλὰς ἑπτὰ καὶ κέρατα δέκα.

The woman was dressed in purple and scarlet, and adorned with gold and precious stones and pearls.[^5] In her hand she held a golden cup full of detestable things[^6] and the impurities of her sexual immorality.

καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἦν περιβεβλημένη πορφυροῦν καὶ κόκκινον, καὶ κεχρυσωμένη χρυσίῳ καὶ λίθῳ τιμίῳ καὶ μαργαρίταις, ἔχουσα ποτήριον χρυσοῦν ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτῆς γέμον βδελυγμάτων καὶ τὰ ἀκάθαρτα τῆς πορνείας αὐτῆς,
On her forehead was written a name, a mystery:[^7] "Babylon the great, the mother of prostitutes and of the detestable things of the earth."
καὶ ἐπὶ τὸ μέτωπον αὐτῆς ὄνομα γεγραμμένον, μυστήριον, Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη, ἡ μήτηρ τῶν πορνῶν καὶ τῶν βδελυγμάτων τῆς γῆς.
And I saw that the woman was drunk with the blood of God's holy people[^8] and with the blood of the witnesses to Jesus.[^9] When I saw her, I was utterly amazed.
καὶ εἶδον τὴν γυναῖκα μεθύουσαν ἐκ τοῦ αἵματος τῶν ἁγίων καὶ ἐκ τοῦ αἵματος τῶν μαρτύρων Ἰησοῦ. Καὶ ἐθαύμασα ἰδὼν αὐτὴν θαῦμα μέγα·
But the angel said to me, "Why are you amazed? I will tell you the mystery of the woman and of the beast that carries her, which has the seven heads and the ten horns.
καὶ εἶπέν μοι ὁ ἄγγελος· Διὰ τί ἐθαύμασας; ἐγὼ ἐρῶ σοι τὸ μυστήριον τῆς γυναικὸς καὶ τοῦ θηρίου τοῦ βαστάζοντος αὐτήν, τοῦ ἔχοντος τὰς ἑπτὰ κεφαλὰς καὶ τὰ δέκα κέρατα·

The beast that you saw was, and is not, and is about to come up out of the abyss and go to destruction. Those who live on the earth, whose names have not been written in the book of life since the foundation of the world, will be amazed when they see the beast, because it was, and is not, and will come.[^10]

τὸ θηρίον ὃ εἶδες ἦν καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν, καὶ μέλλει ἀναβαίνειν ἐκ τῆς ἀβύσσου, καὶ εἰς ἀπώλειαν ὑπάγει· καὶ θαυμασθήσονται οἱ κατοικοῦντες ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ὧν οὐ γέγραπται τὸ ὄνομα ἐπὶ τὸ βιβλίον τῆς ζωῆς ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου, βλεπόντων τὸ θηρίον ὅτι ἦν καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν καὶ παρέσται.
This calls for a mind that has wisdom.[^11] The seven heads are seven mountains, on which the woman is seated.[^12] They are also seven kings.
Ὧδε ὁ νοῦς ὁ ἔχων σοφίαν. αἱ ἑπτὰ κεφαλαὶ ἑπτὰ ὄρη εἰσίν, ὅπου ἡ γυνὴ κάθηται ἐπʼ αὐτῶν. καὶ βασιλεῖς ἑπτά εἰσιν·
Five have fallen, one is, and the other has not yet come; and when he comes, he must remain only a little while.
οἱ πέντε ἔπεσαν, ὁ εἷς ἔστιν, ὁ ἄλλος οὔπω ἦλθεν, καὶ ὅταν ἔλθῃ ὀλίγον αὐτὸν δεῖ μεῖναι,
As for the beast that was and is not, it is itself an eighth king, and it belongs to the seven,[^13] and it goes to destruction.
καὶ τὸ θηρίον ὃ ἦν καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν. καὶ αὐτὸς ὄγδοός ἐστιν καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἑπτά ἐστιν, καὶ εἰς ἀπώλειαν ὑπάγει.
The ten horns that you saw are ten kings who have not yet received a kingdom, but they receive authority as kings for one hour, together with the beast.[^14]
καὶ τὰ δέκα κέρατα ἃ εἶδες δέκα βασιλεῖς εἰσιν, οἵτινες βασιλείαν οὔπω ἔλαβον, ἀλλὰ ἐξουσίαν ὡς βασιλεῖς μίαν ὥραν λαμβάνουσιν μετὰ τοῦ θηρίου.
These are of one mind, and they give their power and authority to the beast.
οὗτοι μίαν γνώμην ἔχουσιν, καὶ τὴν δύναμιν καὶ ἐξουσίαν αὐτῶν τῷ θηρίῳ διδόασιν.
They will make war on the Lamb, and the Lamb will conquer them, for he is Lord of lords and King of kings,[^15] and those with him are called and chosen and faithful."
οὗτοι μετὰ τοῦ ἀρνίου πολεμήσουσιν, καὶ τὸ ἀρνίον νικήσει αὐτούς, ὅτι κύριος κυρίων ἐστὶν καὶ βασιλεὺς βασιλέων, καὶ οἱ μετʼ αὐτοῦ κλητοὶ καὶ ἐκλεκτοὶ καὶ πιστοί.
Then he said to me, "The waters that you saw, where the prostitute is seated, are peoples and crowds and nations and languages.
Καὶ λέγει μοι· Τὰ ὕδατα ἃ εἶδες, οὗ ἡ πόρνη κάθηται, λαοὶ καὶ ὄχλοι εἰσὶν καὶ ἔθνη καὶ γλῶσσαι.
The ten horns that you saw, and the beast, will hate the prostitute. They will make her desolate and naked; they will devour her flesh and burn her up with fire.[^16]
καὶ τὰ δέκα κέρατα ἃ εἶδες καὶ τὸ θηρίον, οὗτοι μισήσουσι τὴν πόρνην, καὶ ἠρημωμένην ποιήσουσιν αὐτὴν καὶ γυμνήν, καὶ τὰς σάρκας αὐτῆς φάγονται, καὶ αὐτὴν κατακαύσουσιν ἐν πυρί·
For God has put it into their hearts to carry out his purpose, by agreeing together to give their kingdom to the beast,[^17] until the words of God are fulfilled.
ὁ γὰρ θεὸς ἔδωκεν εἰς τὰς καρδίας αὐτῶν ποιῆσαι τὴν γνώμην αὐτοῦ, καὶ ποιῆσαι μίαν γνώμην καὶ δοῦναι τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτῶν τῷ θηρίῳ, ἄχρι τελεσθήσονται οἱ λόγοι τοῦ θεοῦ.
The woman whom you saw is the great city that rules over the kings of the earth."
καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἣν εἶδες ἔστιν ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη ἡ ἔχουσα βασιλείαν ἐπὶ τῶν βασιλέων τῆς γῆς.

n.1: Literally "spoke with me, saying".
n.2: Compare Jeremiah 51:13, of Babylon, "You who live by many waters".
n.3: Compare Isaiah 23:17; Jeremiah 51:7, "making the whole earth drunk. The nations drank her wine"; Nahum 3:4.
n.4: Or "in the spirit". See 1:10.
n.5: Literally "gilded with gold and precious stone and pearls".
n.6: Greek *bdelygmata*, "abominations", the word used in the Greek Old Testament for idols and idolatrous practices; also in verse 5. *A golden cup*: compare Jeremiah 51:7, "Babylon was a golden cup in the LORD's hand".
n.7: Or "a name with a hidden meaning". Greek *mysterion*; also in verse 7.
n.8: Literally "of the holy ones", traditionally "of the saints".
n.9: Or "the martyrs of Jesus". Greek *martys*, "witness", the source of the word "martyr".
n.10: Literally "will be present". The words echo, in contrast, the title of God, "who is and who was and who is to come" (1:4, 8).
n.11: Literally "Here is the mind that has wisdom".
n.12: Rome was known as the city of seven hills, and many interpreters see a reference to it here.
n.13: Literally "it is an eighth, and it is from the seven".
n.14: Compare Daniel 7:24, "As for the ten horns, out of this kingdom ten kings will arise".
n.15: Compare Deuteronomy 10:17, "For the LORD your God is God of gods and Lord of lords"; Daniel 2:47.
n.16: Compare Ezekiel 16:37–41 and 23:25–29, where Jerusalem's lovers strip her and leave her naked.
n.17: Literally "to do his purpose, and to do one purpose, and to give their kingdom to the beast".

v: After this I saw another angel coming down from heaven, with great authority, and the earth was lit up by his glory.[^1]
Μετὰ ταῦτα εἶδον ἄλλον ἄγγελον καταβαίνοντα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, ἔχοντα ἐξουσίαν μεγάλην, καὶ ἡ γῆ ἐφωτίσθη ἐκ τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ.

He called out with a mighty voice, "Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great![^2] She has become a dwelling place of demons, a haunt[^3] for every unclean spirit, a haunt for every unclean bird, and a haunt for every unclean beast,[^4] unclean and hated.[^5]

καὶ ἔκραξεν ἐν ἰσχυρᾷ φωνῇ λέγων· Ἔπεσεν, ἔπεσεν Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη, καὶ ἐγένετο κατοικητήριον δαιμονίων καὶ φυλακὴ παντὸς πνεύματος ἀκαθάρτου καὶ φυλακὴ παντὸς ὀρνέου ἀκαθάρτου καὶ φυλακὴ παντὸς θηρίου ἀκαθάρτου καὶ μεμισημένου,

For all the nations have fallen[^6] because of the wine of the passion of her sexual immorality, and the kings of the earth have committed sexual immorality with her, and the merchants of the earth have grown rich from the power of her luxury."[^7]
ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ οἴνου τοῦ θυμοῦ τῆς πορνείας αὐτῆς πέπτωκαν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς μετʼ αὐτῆς ἐπόρνευσαν, καὶ οἱ ἔμποροι τῆς γῆς ἐκ τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ στρήνους αὐτῆς ἐπλούτησαν.
Then I heard another voice from heaven saying, "Come out of her, my people,[^8] so that you do not take part in her sins, and so that you do not receive any of her plagues.
Καὶ ἤκουσα ἄλλην φωνὴν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ λέγουσαν· Ἐξέλθατε, ὁ λαός μου, ἐξ αὐτῆς, ἵνα μὴ συγκοινωνήσητε ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις αὐτῆς, καὶ ἐκ τῶν πληγῶν αὐτῆς ἵνα μὴ λάβητε·
For her sins are piled up to heaven,[^9] and God has remembered her crimes.
ὅτι ἐκολλήθησαν αὐτῆς αἱ ἁμαρτίαι ἄχρι τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἐμνημόνευσεν ὁ θεὸς τὰ ἀδικήματα αὐτῆς.
Pay her back as she herself has paid others,[^10] and repay her double for her works. In the cup she mixed, mix her a double portion.[^11]
ἀπόδοτε αὐτῇ ὡς καὶ αὐτὴ ἀπέδωκεν, καὶ διπλώσατε τὰ διπλᾶ κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῆς· ἐν τῷ ποτηρίῳ ᾧ ἐκέρασεν κεράσατε αὐτῇ διπλοῦν·
As much as she glorified herself and lived in luxury, give her that much torment and grief. For in her heart she says, 'I sit as a queen. I am no widow, and I will never see grief.'[^12]
ὅσα ἐδόξασεν αὑτὴν καὶ ἐστρηνίασεν, τοσοῦτον δότε αὐτῇ βασανισμὸν καὶ πένθος. ὅτι ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτῆς λέγει ὅτι Κάθημαι βασίλισσα, καὶ χήρα οὐκ εἰμί, καὶ πένθος οὐ μὴ ἴδω.
That is why her plagues will come in a single day: death and grief and famine. And she will be burned up with fire, for mighty is the Lord God who judges her.[^13]
διὰ τοῦτο ἐν μιᾷ ἡμέρᾳ ἥξουσιν αἱ πληγαὶ αὐτῆς, θάνατος καὶ πένθος καὶ λιμός, καὶ ἐν πυρὶ κατακαυθήσεται· ὅτι ἰσχυρὸς κύριος ὁ θεὸς ὁ κρίνας αὐτήν.
The kings of the earth who committed sexual immorality and lived in luxury with her will weep and mourn over her when they see the smoke of her burning.[^14]
Καὶ κλαύσουσιν καὶ κόψονται ἐπʼ αὐτὴν οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς οἱ μετʼ αὐτῆς πορνεύσαντες καὶ στρηνιάσαντες, ὅταν βλέπωσιν τὸν καπνὸν τῆς πυρώσεως αὐτῆς,
They will stand far off, in fear of her torment, and say, 'Woe, woe,[^15] you great city, Babylon, you mighty city! In one hour your judgment has come.'
ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἑστηκότες διὰ τὸν φόβον τοῦ βασανισμοῦ αὐτῆς λέγοντες· Οὐαὶ οὐαί, ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη, Βαβυλὼν ἡ πόλις ἡ ἰσχυρά, ὅτι μιᾷ ὥρᾳ ἦλθεν ἡ κρίσις σου.
And the merchants of the earth weep and mourn over her, because no one buys their cargo anymore:[^16]
Καὶ οἱ ἔμποροι τῆς γῆς κλαίουσιν καὶ πενθοῦσιν ἐπʼ αὐτήν, ὅτι τὸν γόμον αὐτῶν οὐδεὶς ἀγοράζει οὐκέτι,

cargo of gold, silver, precious stones and pearls; fine linen, purple, silk and scarlet; all kinds of citron wood,[^17] all kinds of articles of ivory, all kinds of articles of costly wood, bronze, iron and marble;

γόμον χρυσοῦ καὶ ἀργύρου καὶ λίθου τιμίου καὶ μαργαριτῶν καὶ βυσσίνου καὶ πορφύρας καὶ σιρικοῦ καὶ κοκκίνου, καὶ πᾶν ξύλον θύϊνον καὶ πᾶν σκεῦος ἐλεφάντινον καὶ πᾶν σκεῦος ἐκ ξύλου τιμιωτάτου καὶ χαλκοῦ καὶ σιδήρου καὶ μαρμάρου,
cinnamon, spice,[^18] incense, myrrh[^19] and frankincense; wine, olive oil, fine flour and wheat; cattle and sheep; horses and carriages; and slaves, that is, human lives.[^20]
καὶ κιννάμωμον καὶ ἄμωμον καὶ θυμιάματα καὶ μύρον καὶ λίβανον καὶ οἶνον καὶ ἔλαιον καὶ σεμίδαλιν καὶ σῖτον καὶ κτήνη καὶ πρόβατα, καὶ ἵππων καὶ ῥεδῶν καὶ σωμάτων, καὶ ψυχὰς ἀνθρώπων.
The fruit that your soul longed for has gone from you, and all your luxury and your splendor have perished from you, and they will never be found again.[^21]
καὶ ἡ ὀπώρα σου τῆς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς ψυχῆς ἀπῆλθεν ἀπὸ σοῦ, καὶ πάντα τὰ λιπαρὰ καὶ τὰ λαμπρὰ ἀπώλετο ἀπὸ σοῦ, καὶ οὐκέτι οὐ μὴ αὐτὰ εὑρήσουσιν.
The merchants of these things, who grew rich from her, will stand far off in fear of her torment, weeping and mourning,
οἱ ἔμποροι τούτων, οἱ πλουτήσαντες ἀπʼ αὐτῆς, ἀπὸ μακρόθεν στήσονται διὰ τὸν φόβον τοῦ βασανισμοῦ αὐτῆς κλαίοντες καὶ πενθοῦντες,
and saying, 'Woe, woe, the great city, which was dressed in fine linen and purple and scarlet, and adorned with gold and precious stones and pearls!
λέγοντες· Οὐαὶ οὐαί, ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη, ἡ περιβεβλημένη βύσσινον καὶ πορφυροῦν καὶ κόκκινον καὶ κεχρυσωμένη χρυσίῳ καὶ λίθῳ τιμίῳ καὶ μαργαρίτῃ,
For in one hour such great wealth has been laid waste!' And every ship's captain and every passenger,[^22] and sailors, and all who make their living from the sea, stood far off
ὅτι μιᾷ ὥρᾳ ἠρημώθη ὁ τοσοῦτος πλοῦτος. Καὶ πᾶς κυβερνήτης καὶ πᾶς ὁ ἐπὶ τόπον πλέων, καὶ ναῦται καὶ ὅσοι τὴν θάλασσαν ἐργάζονται, ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἔστησαν
and cried out as they saw the smoke of her burning, 'What city was like the great city?'[^23]
καὶ ἔκραξαν βλέποντες τὸν καπνὸν τῆς πυρώσεως αὐτῆς λέγοντες· Τίς ὁμοία τῇ πόλει τῇ μεγάλῃ;

And they threw dust on their heads[^24] and cried out, weeping and mourning, 'Woe, woe, the great city, where all who had ships at sea grew rich from her wealth! For in one hour she has been laid waste.'

καὶ ἔβαλον χοῦν ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν καὶ ἔκραξαν κλαίοντες καὶ πενθοῦντες λέγοντες· Οὐαὶ οὐαί, ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη, ἐν ᾗ ἐπλούτησαν πάντες οἱ ἔχοντες τὰ πλοῖα ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ ἐκ τῆς τιμιότητος αὐτῆς, ὅτι μιᾷ ὥρᾳ ἠρημώθη.
Rejoice over her, heaven, and you, God's holy people[^25] and apostles and prophets, for God has given judgment for you against her."[^26]
Εὐφραίνου ἐπʼ αὐτῇ, οὐρανέ, καὶ οἱ ἅγιοι καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ προφῆται, ὅτι ἔκρινεν ὁ θεὸς τὸ κρίμα ὑμῶν ἐξ αὐτῆς.
Then a mighty angel picked up a stone like a great millstone and threw it into the sea, saying, "With such violence Babylon the great city will be thrown down, and will never be found again.[^27]
Καὶ ἦρεν εἷς ἄγγελος ἰσχυρὸς λίθον ὡς μύλινον μέγαν, καὶ ἔβαλεν εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν λέγων· Οὕτως ὁρμήματι βληθήσεται Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη πόλις, καὶ οὐ μὴ εὑρεθῇ ἔτι.

The sound of harpists and musicians, of flute players and trumpeters, will never be heard in you again. No craftsman of any craft will ever be found in you again. The sound of the millstone will never be heard in you again.
καὶ φωνὴ κιθαρῳδῶν καὶ μουσικῶν καὶ αὐλητῶν καὶ σαλπιστῶν οὐ μὴ ἀκουσθῇ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι, καὶ πᾶς τεχνίτης πάσης τέχνης οὐ μὴ εὑρεθῇ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι, καὶ φωνὴ μύλου οὐ μὴ ἀκουσθῇ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι,

The light of a lamp will never shine in you again. The voice of bridegroom and bride will never be heard in you again.[^28] For your merchants were the great ones of the earth,[^29] and all the nations were deceived by your sorcery.
καὶ φῶς λύχνου οὐ μὴ φάνῃ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι, καὶ φωνὴ νυμφίου καὶ νύμφης οὐ μὴ ἀκουσθῇ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι· ὅτι οἱ ἔμποροί σου ἦσαν οἱ μεγιστᾶνες τῆς γῆς, ὅτι ἐν τῇ φαρμακείᾳ σου ἐπλανήθησαν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη,
And in her was found the blood of prophets and of God's holy people, and of all who have been slaughtered on the earth."[^30]
καὶ ἐν αὐτῇ αἷμα προφητῶν καὶ ἁγίων εὑρέθη καὶ πάντων τῶν ἐσφαγμένων ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.

n.1: Compare Ezekiel 43:2, "and the earth shone with his glory".
n.2: See 14:8; Isaiah 21:9. Many manuscripts have "Fallen" only once.
n.3: Or "a prison"; also later in the verse.
n.4: The SBLGNT here follows NA28; other editions leave out "a haunt for every unclean beast".
n.5: Compare Isaiah 13:21–22; 34:11–15; Jeremiah 50:39; 51:37, where wild creatures haunt the ruins of Babylon and Edom.
n.6: Some manuscripts read "have drunk". *Passion*: see the note on 14:8.
n.7: Or "the power of her self-indulgence", her excessive wealth and display.
n.8: Jeremiah 51:45, "Go out from her midst, my people!"; compare Isaiah 48:20; 52:11; Jeremiah 50:8; 51:6.
n.9: Compare Jeremiah 51:9, "her judgment reaches to the heavens".
n.10: Compare Psalm 137:8; Jeremiah 50:29, "Repay her for her deeds; do to her just as she has done."
n.11: Literally "double the double according to her works; in the cup in which she mixed, mix for her double". Compare Jeremiah 16:18.
n.12: Compare Isaiah 47:7–8, "I will be queen forever … I will never sit as a widow".
n.13: Compare Isaiah 47:9, "Both of these will come on you in a moment, in a single day"; Jeremiah 50:34, "But their Redeemer is strong".
n.14: Verses 9–19 draw on the lament over Tyre in Ezekiel 26–27.
n.15: Greek *ouai*, a cry of grief and warning, like the prophets' *hoy* ("woe"); also in verses 16 and 19.
n.16: Compare Ezekiel 27:12–24, the list of Tyre's trade.
n.17: A fragrant wood from North Africa, prized for fine furniture.
n.18: Greek *amomon*, a spice plant from India. Many manuscripts leave out "spice".
n.20: Literally "and bodies, and souls of human beings". Greek *somata*, "bodies", was a common term for slaves. Compare Ezekiel 27:13, "They gave human beings … for your merchandise."
n.21: Literally "and they will never find them again". Many manuscripts read "and you will never find them again".
n.22: Literally "everyone who sails to a place"; the meaning is uncertain.
n.23: Compare Ezekiel 27:32, "Who was like Tyre, like one silenced in the middle of the sea?"
n.24: Compare Ezekiel 27:30, "They will throw dust on their heads".
n.25: Literally "the holy ones", traditionally "the saints"; also in verse 24.
n.26: Literally "God has judged your judgment from her". It is not certain where the voice of verse 4 stops speaking; this translation takes verses 4–20 as its words. Compare Jeremiah 51:48, "Then heaven and earth and all that is in them will shout for joy over Babylon".

n.30: Compare Jeremiah 51:49, "as the slain of all the earth have fallen because of Babylon".

v: After this I heard what sounded like the loud voice of a great crowd in heaven, saying, "Hallelujah![^1] Salvation and glory and power belong to our God,
Μετὰ ταῦτα ἤκουσα ὡς φωνὴν μεγάλην ὄχλου πολλοῦ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ λεγόντων· Ἁλληλουϊά· ἡ σωτηρία καὶ ἡ δόξα καὶ ἡ δύναμις τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν,
for his judgments are true and just.[^2] He has judged the great prostitute who corrupted the earth with her sexual immorality, and he has avenged on her the blood of his servants."[^3]
ὅτι ἀληθιναὶ καὶ δίκαιαι αἱ κρίσεις αὐτοῦ· ὅτι ἔκρινεν τὴν πόρνην τὴν μεγάλην ἥτις ἔφθειρεν τὴν γῆν ἐν τῇ πορνείᾳ αὐτῆς, καὶ ἐξεδίκησεν τὸ αἷμα τῶν δούλων αὐτοῦ ἐκ χειρὸς αὐτῆς.
And a second time they said, "Hallelujah! The smoke from her goes up forever and ever."[^4]
καὶ δεύτερον εἴρηκαν· Ἁλληλουϊά· καὶ ὁ καπνὸς αὐτῆς ἀναβαίνει εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων.
Then the twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell down and worshiped God, who is seated on the throne, saying, "Amen. Hallelujah!"[^5]
καὶ ἔπεσαν οἱ πρεσβύτεροι οἱ εἴκοσι τέσσαρες καὶ τὰ τέσσαρα ζῷα, καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ θεῷ τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπὶ τῷ θρόνῳ λέγοντες· Ἀμήν, Ἁλληλουϊά.
And a voice came from the throne, saying, "Praise our God, all you his servants, you who fear him, small and great."[^6]
Καὶ φωνὴ ἀπὸ τοῦ θρόνου ἐξῆλθεν λέγουσα· Αἰνεῖτε τῷ θεῷ ἡμῶν, πάντες οἱ δοῦλοι αὐτοῦ, καὶ οἱ φοβούμενοι αὐτόν, οἱ μικροὶ καὶ οἱ μεγάλοι.

Then I heard what sounded like the voice of a great crowd, like the sound of many waters and like the sound of mighty peals of thunder, saying, "Hallelujah! For the Lord God, the Almighty, reigns.[^7]
καὶ ἤκουσα ὡς φωνὴν ὄχλου πολλοῦ καὶ ὡς φωνὴν ὑδάτων πολλῶν καὶ ὡς φωνὴν βροντῶν ἰσχυρῶν, λεγόντων· Ἁλληλουϊά, ὅτι ἐβασίλευσεν κύριος, ὁ θεός, ὁ παντοκράτωρ.
Let us rejoice and be glad, and we will give him the glory,[^8] for the wedding of the Lamb has come, and his bride[^9] has made herself ready.
χαίρωμεν καὶ ἀγαλλιῶμεν, καὶ δώσομεν τὴν δόξαν αὐτῷ, ὅτι ἦλθεν ὁ γάμος τοῦ ἀρνίου, καὶ ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ ἡτοίμασεν ἑαυτήν,
She has been given fine linen, bright and clean, to wear." For the fine linen is the righteous deeds[^10] of God's holy people.[^11]
καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῇ ἵνα περιβάληται βύσσινον λαμπρὸν καθαρόν, τὸ γὰρ βύσσινον τὰ δικαιώματα τῶν ἁγίων ἐστίν.
Then he said to me,[^12] "Write: Blessed are those who are invited to the wedding banquet of the Lamb." And he said to me, "These are the true words of God."
Καὶ λέγει μοι· Γράψον· Μακάριοι οἱ εἰς τὸ δεῖπνον τοῦ γάμου τοῦ ἀρνίου κεκλημένοι. καὶ λέγει μοι· Οὗτοι οἱ λόγοι ἀληθινοὶ τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσιν.

Then I fell at his feet to worship him, but he said to me, "Don't do that! I am a fellow servant with you and with your brothers and sisters[^13] who hold to the testimony of Jesus.[^14] Worship God! For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy."

καὶ ἔπεσα ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ προσκυνῆσαι αὐτῷ. καὶ λέγει μοι· Ὅρα μή· σύνδουλός σού εἰμι καὶ τῶν ἀδελφῶν σου τῶν ἐχόντων τὴν μαρτυρίαν Ἰησοῦ· τῷ θεῷ προσκύνησον· ἡ γὰρ μαρτυρία Ἰησοῦ ἐστιν τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς προφητείας.
Then I saw heaven standing open, and there was a white horse. Its rider is called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he judges and makes war.[^15]
Καὶ εἶδον τὸν οὐρανὸν ἠνεῳγμένον, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἵππος λευκός, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπʼ αὐτὸν πιστὸς καλούμενος καὶ ἀληθινός, καὶ ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ κρίνει καὶ πολεμεῖ.
His eyes were a flame of fire,[^16] and on his head were many diadems. He had a name written that no one knows except he himself.[^17]
οἱ δὲ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῦ φλὸξ πυρός, καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ διαδήματα πολλά, ἔχων ὄνομα γεγραμμένον ὃ οὐδεὶς οἶδεν εἰ μὴ αὐτός,
He was dressed in a robe dipped in blood,[^18] and his name is called the Word of God.[^19]
καὶ περιβεβλημένος ἱμάτιον βεβαμμένον αἵματι, καὶ κέκληται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ὁ Λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ.
The armies of heaven, dressed in fine linen, white and clean, were following him on white horses.
καὶ τὰ στρατεύματα τὰ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ ἐφʼ ἵπποις λευκοῖς, ἐνδεδυμένοι βύσσινον λευκὸν καθαρόν.

Out of his mouth came a sharp sword[^20] with which to strike down the nations,[^21] and he will rule them with an iron rod.[^22] He treads the winepress of the wine of the fury of the anger of God Almighty.[^23]

καὶ ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ ἐκπορεύεται ῥομφαία ὀξεῖα, ἵνα ἐν αὐτῇ πατάξῃ τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ αὐτὸς ποιμανεῖ αὐτοὺς ἐν ῥάβδῳ σιδηρᾷ· καὶ αὐτὸς πατεῖ τὴν ληνὸν τοῦ οἴνου τοῦ θυμοῦ τῆς ὀργῆς τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ παντοκράτορος.
On his robe and on his thigh he has a name written: King of kings and Lord of lords.[^24]
καὶ ἔχει ἐπὶ τὸ ἱμάτιον καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν μηρὸν αὐτοῦ ὄνομα γεγραμμένον· Βασιλεὺς βασιλέων καὶ κύριος κυρίων.
Then I saw an angel[^25] standing in the sun, and he called out with a loud voice to all the birds flying in midheaven, "Come, gather for the great banquet of God,
Καὶ εἶδον ἕνα ἄγγελον ἑστῶτα ἐν τῷ ἡλίῳ, καὶ ἔκραξεν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγων πᾶσι τοῖς ὀρνέοις τοῖς πετομένοις ἐν μεσουρανήματι· Δεῦτε συνάχθητε εἰς τὸ δεῖπνον τὸ μέγα τοῦ θεοῦ,
to eat the flesh of kings, the flesh of generals,[^26] the flesh of the mighty, the flesh of horses and their riders, and the flesh of all people, free and slave, small and great."[^27]
ἵνα φάγητε σάρκας βασιλέων καὶ σάρκας χιλιάρχων καὶ σάρκας ἰσχυρῶν καὶ σάρκας ἵππων καὶ τῶν καθημένων ἐπʼ αὐτῶν, καὶ σάρκας πάντων ἐλευθέρων τε καὶ δούλων καὶ μικρῶν καὶ μεγάλων.
Then I saw the beast and the kings of the earth and their armies gathered to make war against the rider on the horse and against his army.[^28]
καὶ εἶδον τὸ θηρίον καὶ τοὺς βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς καὶ τὰ στρατεύματα αὐτῶν συνηγμένα ποιῆσαι τὸν πόλεμον μετὰ τοῦ καθημένου ἐπὶ τοῦ ἵππου καὶ μετὰ τοῦ στρατεύματος αὐτοῦ.

But the beast was captured, and with it the false prophet who had performed the signs on its behalf,[^29] by which he deceived those who had received the mark of the beast and those who worshiped its image. The two of them were thrown alive into the lake of fire that burns with sulfur.[^30]

καὶ ἐπιάσθη τὸ θηρίον καὶ μετʼ αὐτοῦ ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης ὁ ποιήσας τὰ σημεῖα ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ, ἐν οἷς ἐπλάνησεν τοὺς λαβόντας τὸ χάραγμα τοῦ θηρίου καὶ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας τῇ εἰκόνι αὐτοῦ· ζῶντες ἐβλήθησαν οἱ δύο εἰς τὴν λίμνην τοῦ πυρὸς τῆς καιομένης ἐν θείῳ.
The rest were killed by the sword that came out of the mouth of the rider on the horse, and all the birds gorged themselves on their flesh.
καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ ἀπεκτάνθησαν ἐν τῇ ῥομφαίᾳ τοῦ καθημένου ἐπὶ τοῦ ἵππου τῇ ἐξελθούσῃ ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ, καὶ πάντα τὰ ὄρνεα ἐχορτάσθησαν ἐκ τῶν σαρκῶν αὐτῶν.

n.1: Greek *hallelouia*, from the Hebrew *hallelu-yah*, "Praise Yah!" (as in Psalms 104:35; 106:48; 146–150). *Yah* is a short form of God's personal name, YHWH ("the LORD"). In the New Testament the word occurs only in verses 1–6 of this chapter.
n.3: Literally "from her hand". Compare Deuteronomy 32:43, "for he will avenge the blood of his servants"; 2 Kings 9:7, of Jezebel.
n.4: Compare Isaiah 34:10, "its smoke will go up forever". See 14:11.
n.5: Compare Psalm 106:48, "Let all the people say, 'Amen!' Praise Yah!"
n.6: Compare Psalm 135:1, "praise him, you servants of the LORD"; 135:20, "You who fear the LORD, bless the LORD!"; 115:13.
n.7: Or "has begun to reign". Compare Psalms 93:1; 97:1; 99:1, "The LORD reigns!", where the Greek Old Testament has the same verb. In the Hebrew, "the Lord" there is God's personal name, YHWH ("the LORD"). The SBLGNT here follows the margin of Westcott and Hort; the other editions read "the Lord our God, the Almighty".
n.8: The SBLGNT here follows Westcott and Hort; other editions read "and let us give him the glory".
n.9: Literally "his wife". Compare Isaiah 54:5–6; 62:5; Hosea 2:21–22 (2:19–20 in most English Bibles), where God is the husband of his people.
n.10: Greek *dikaiomata*, "righteous acts". Compare Isaiah 61:10, "he has clothed me with garments of salvation and wrapped me in a robe of righteousness".
n.11: Literally "of the holy ones", traditionally "of the saints".
n.12: That is, the angel, probably the angel of 17:1.
n.13: Greek *adelphoi*, "brothers", used of the believers, men and women alike.
n.14: Or "the testimony about Jesus"; also later in the verse.
n.15: Compare Isaiah 11:4, "He will judge the poor with righteousness"; Psalm 96:13.
n.16: Some manuscripts read "like a flame of fire", as in 1:14.
n.17: Many manuscripts read "He had names written, and a name written that no one knows except he himself."
n.18: Some manuscripts read "sprinkled with blood". Compare Isaiah 63:1–3, "Why is your clothing red, and your garments like those of one who treads in the winepress?"
n.20: Many manuscripts read "a sharp two-edged sword", as in 1:16.
n.21: Compare Isaiah 11:4, "He will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth".
n.23: Compare Isaiah 63:3, "I have trodden the winepress alone". See 14:19–20.

v: Then I saw an angel coming down from heaven, holding in his hand the key to the abyss[^1] and a great chain.
Καὶ εἶδον ἄγγελον καταβαίνοντα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, ἔχοντα τὴν κλεῖν τῆς ἀβύσσου καὶ ἅλυσιν μεγάλην ἐπὶ τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ.
He seized the dragon, that ancient serpent, who is the devil and Satan,[^2] and bound him for a thousand years.
καὶ ἐκράτησεν τὸν δράκοντα, ὁ ὄφις ὁ ἀρχαῖος, ὅς ἐστιν Διάβολος καὶ ὁ Σατανᾶς, καὶ ἔδησεν αὐτὸν χίλια ἔτη,
He threw him into the abyss, and locked it and sealed it over him, so that he would no longer deceive the nations until the thousand years were ended. After that he must be released for a short time.
καὶ ἔβαλεν αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν ἄβυσσον, καὶ ἔκλεισεν καὶ ἐσφράγισεν ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ, ἵνα μὴ πλανήσῃ ἔτι τὰ ἔθνη, ἄχρι τελεσθῇ τὰ χίλια ἔτη· μετὰ ταῦτα δεῖ λυθῆναι αὐτὸν μικρὸν χρόνον.

Then I saw thrones, and those seated on them were given authority to judge.[^3] I also saw the souls of those who had been beheaded because of their testimony to Jesus[^4] and because of the word of God, and those who had not worshiped the beast or its image and had not received its mark on their foreheads or on their hands. They came to life and reigned with the Messiah[^5] for a thousand years.

Καὶ εἶδον θρόνους, καὶ ἐκάθισαν ἐπʼ αὐτούς, καὶ κρίμα ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς, καὶ τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν πεπελεκισμένων διὰ τὴν μαρτυρίαν Ἰησοῦ καὶ διὰ τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ οἵτινες οὐ προσεκύνησαν τὸ θηρίον οὐδὲ τὴν εἰκόνα αὐτοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἔλαβον τὸ χάραγμα ἐπὶ τὸ μέτωπον καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν χεῖρα αὐτῶν· καὶ ἔζησαν καὶ ἐβασίλευσαν μετὰ τοῦ χριστοῦ χίλια ἔτη.
The rest of the dead did not come to life until the thousand years were ended. This is the first resurrection.
οἱ λοιποὶ τῶν νεκρῶν οὐκ ἔζησαν ἄχρι τελεσθῇ τὰ χίλια ἔτη. αὕτη ἡ ἀνάστασις ἡ πρώτη.

Blessed and holy is the one who has a share in the first resurrection. Over these the second death has no authority, but they will be priests of God and of the Messiah, and they will reign with him for a thousand years.
μακάριος καὶ ἅγιος ὁ ἔχων μέρος ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει τῇ πρώτῃ· ἐπὶ τούτων ὁ δεύτερος θάνατος οὐκ ἔχει ἐξουσίαν, ἀλλʼ ἔσονται ἱερεῖς τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ χριστοῦ, καὶ βασιλεύσουσιν μετʼ αὐτοῦ χίλια ἔτη.
When the thousand years are ended, Satan will be released from his prison,
Καὶ ὅταν τελεσθῇ τὰ χίλια ἔτη, λυθήσεται ὁ Σατανᾶς ἐκ τῆς φυλακῆς αὐτοῦ,
and he will go out to deceive the nations at the four corners of the earth, Gog and Magog,[^6] to gather them for battle. Their number is like the sand of the sea.
καὶ ἐξελεύσεται πλανῆσαι τὰ ἔθνη τὰ ἐν ταῖς τέσσαρσι γωνίαις τῆς γῆς, τὸν Γὼγ καὶ Μαγώγ, συναγαγεῖν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν πόλεμον, ὧν ὁ ἀριθμὸς αὐτῶν ὡς ἡ ἄμμος τῆς θαλάσσης.
They marched up across the breadth of the earth and surrounded the camp of God's holy people[^7] and the beloved city. But fire came down from heaven[^8] and consumed them.
καὶ ἀνέβησαν ἐπὶ τὸ πλάτος τῆς γῆς, καὶ ἐκύκλευσαν τὴν παρεμβολὴν τῶν ἁγίων καὶ τὴν πόλιν τὴν ἠγαπημένην. καὶ κατέβη πῦρ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ κατέφαγεν αὐτούς·
And the devil, who had deceived them, was thrown into the lake of fire and sulfur, where the beast and the false prophet also were,[^9] and they will be tormented day and night forever and ever.
καὶ ὁ διάβολος ὁ πλανῶν αὐτοὺς ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν λίμνην τοῦ πυρὸς καὶ θείου, ὅπου καὶ τὸ θηρίον καὶ ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης, καὶ βασανισθήσονται ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτὸς εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων.
Then I saw a great white throne and the One seated on it. Earth and heaven fled from his presence, and no place was found for them.[^10]
Καὶ εἶδον θρόνον μέγαν λευκὸν καὶ τὸν καθήμενον ἐπʼ αὐτοῦ, οὗ ἀπὸ τοῦ προσώπου ἔφυγεν ἡ γῆ καὶ ὁ οὐρανός, καὶ τόπος οὐχ εὑρέθη αὐτοῖς.

And I saw the dead, great and small, standing before the throne, and books[^11] were opened. Another book was opened, which is the book of life.[^12] The dead were judged according to their works, by what was written in the books.[^13]

καὶ εἶδον τοὺς νεκρούς, τοὺς μεγάλους καὶ τοὺς μικρούς, ἑστῶτας ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου, καὶ βιβλία ἠνοίχθησαν· καὶ ἄλλο βιβλίον ἠνοίχθη, ὅ ἐστιν τῆς ζωῆς· καὶ ἐκρίθησαν οἱ νεκροὶ ἐκ τῶν γεγραμμένων ἐν τοῖς βιβλίοις κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν.
The sea gave up the dead that were in it, and Death and Hades[^14] gave up the dead that were in them, and each person was judged according to their works.
καὶ ἔδωκεν ἡ θάλασσα τοὺς νεκροὺς τοὺς ἐν αὐτῇ, καὶ ὁ θάνατος καὶ ὁ ᾅδης ἔδωκαν τοὺς νεκροὺς τοὺς ἐν αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἐκρίθησαν ἕκαστος κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν.
Then Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death, the lake of fire.
καὶ ὁ θάνατος καὶ ὁ ᾅδης ἐβλήθησαν εἰς τὴν λίμνην τοῦ πυρός. οὗτος ὁ θάνατος ὁ δεύτερός ἐστιν, ἡ λίμνη τοῦ πυρός.
And anyone who was not found written in the book of life was thrown into the lake of fire.
καὶ εἴ τις οὐχ εὑρέθη ἐν τῇ βίβλῳ τῆς ζωῆς γεγραμμένος, ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν λίμνην τοῦ πυρός.

n.1: See 9:1.
n.2: Many manuscripts add "who deceives the whole world", as in 12:9.
n.3: Literally "and they sat on them, and judgment was given to them". Compare Daniel 7:9, "thrones were set in place", and 7:22, "judgment was given in favor of the holy ones of the Most High".
n.4: Or "the testimony of Jesus". See 1:2.
n.5: Greek *tou christou*, "the Christ"; also in verse 6. See 11:15.

n.7: Literally "the holy ones", traditionally "the saints".

n.10: Compare Daniel 2:35, "not a trace of them could be found".

n.13: Compare Psalm 62:13 (62:12 in most English Bibles), "For you repay each person according to what he has done"; Jeremiah 17:10.

v: Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth,[^1] for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away, and the sea was no more.
Καὶ εἶδον οὐρανὸν καινὸν καὶ γῆν καινήν· ὁ γὰρ πρῶτος οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ πρώτη γῆ ἀπῆλθαν, καὶ ἡ θάλασσα οὐκ ἔστιν ἔτι.
And I saw the holy city, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.[^2]
καὶ τὴν πόλιν τὴν ἁγίαν Ἰερουσαλὴμ καινὴν εἶδον καταβαίνουσαν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, ἡτοιμασμένην ὡς νύμφην κεκοσμημένην τῷ ἀνδρὶ αὐτῆς.
And I heard a loud voice from the throne[^3] saying, "Look, God's dwelling[^4] is with humankind. He will dwell with them, and they will be his peoples,[^5] and God himself will be with them.[^6]
καὶ ἤκουσα φωνῆς μεγάλης ἐκ τοῦ θρόνου λεγούσης· Ἰδοὺ ἡ σκηνὴ τοῦ θεοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ σκηνώσει μετʼ αὐτῶν, καὶ αὐτοὶ λαοὶ αὐτοῦ ἔσονται, καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ θεὸς μετʼ αὐτῶν ἔσται,
He will wipe away every tear from their eyes.[^7] Death will be no more, and there will be no more mourning or crying or pain. The former things have passed away."[^8]
καὶ ἐξαλείψει πᾶν δάκρυον ἐκ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν, καὶ ὁ θάνατος οὐκ ἔσται ἔτι· οὔτε πένθος οὔτε κραυγὴ οὔτε πόνος οὐκ ἔσται ἔτι. τὰ πρῶτα ἀπῆλθαν.
Then the One seated on the throne said, "Look, I am making all things new."[^9] And he said,[^10] "Write this, for these words are trustworthy and true."
Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τῷ θρόνῳ· Ἰδοὺ καινὰ ποιῶ πάντα. καὶ λέγει· Γράψον, ὅτι οὗτοι οἱ λόγοι πιστοὶ καὶ ἀληθινοί εἰσιν.
Then he said to me, "They are done![^11] I am the Alpha and the Omega,[^12] the beginning and the end. To the thirsty I will give water from the spring of the water of life, without cost.[^13]
καὶ εἶπέν μοι· Γέγοναν. ἐγὼ τὸ Ἄλφα καὶ τὸ Ὦ, ἡ ἀρχὴ καὶ τὸ τέλος. ἐγὼ τῷ διψῶντι δώσω ἐκ τῆς πηγῆς τοῦ ὕδατος τῆς ζωῆς δωρεάν.
The one who conquers will inherit these things, and I will be his God, and he will be my son.[^14]
ὁ νικῶν κληρονομήσει ταῦτα, καὶ ἔσομαι αὐτῷ θεὸς καὶ αὐτὸς ἔσται μοι υἱός.

But as for the cowardly, the faithless,[^15] the detestable, murderers, the sexually immoral, sorcerers, idolaters and all liars, their share will be in the lake that burns with fire and sulfur, which is the second death."

τοῖς δὲ δειλοῖς καὶ ἀπίστοις καὶ ἐβδελυγμένοις καὶ φονεῦσι καὶ πόρνοις καὶ φαρμάκοις καὶ εἰδωλολάτραις καὶ πᾶσι τοῖς ψευδέσιν τὸ μέρος αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ λίμνῃ τῇ καιομένῃ πυρὶ καὶ θείῳ, ὅ ἐστιν ὁ θάνατος ὁ δεύτερος.
Then one of the seven angels who had the seven bowls full of the seven last plagues came and said to me,[^16] "Come, I will show you the bride, the wife of the Lamb."
Καὶ ἦλθεν εἷς ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλων τῶν ἐχόντων τὰς ἑπτὰ φιάλας, τῶν γεμόντων τῶν ἑπτὰ πληγῶν τῶν ἐσχάτων, καὶ ἐλάλησεν μετʼ ἐμοῦ λέγων· Δεῦρο, δείξω σοι τὴν νύμφην τὴν γυναῖκα τοῦ ἀρνίου.
And he carried me away in the Spirit[^17] to a great, high mountain,[^18] and showed me the holy city Jerusalem[^19] coming down out of heaven from God,
καὶ ἀπήνεγκέν με ἐν πνεύματι ἐπὶ ὄρος μέγα καὶ ὑψηλόν, καὶ ἔδειξέν μοι τὴν πόλιν τὴν ἁγίαν Ἰερουσαλὴμ καταβαίνουσαν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ,
having the glory of God.[^20] Its radiance was like a most precious stone, like jasper, clear as crystal.
ἔχουσαν τὴν δόξαν τοῦ θεοῦ· ὁ φωστὴρ αὐτῆς ὅμοιος λίθῳ τιμιωτάτῳ, ὡς λίθῳ ἰάσπιδι κρυσταλλίζοντι·
It had a great, high wall with twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names were inscribed on them, those of the twelve tribes of the Israelites.[^21]
ἔχουσα τεῖχος μέγα καὶ ὑψηλόν, ἔχουσα πυλῶνας δώδεκα, καὶ ἐπὶ τοῖς πυλῶσιν ἀγγέλους δώδεκα, καὶ ὀνόματα ἐπιγεγραμμένα ἅ ἐστιν τῶν δώδεκα φυλῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ·
There were three gates on the east, three gates on the north, three gates on the south and three gates on the west.
ἀπὸ ἀνατολῆς πυλῶνες τρεῖς, καὶ ἀπὸ βορρᾶ πυλῶνες τρεῖς, καὶ ἀπὸ νότου πυλῶνες τρεῖς, καὶ ἀπὸ δυσμῶν πυλῶνες τρεῖς·
The wall of the city had twelve foundations, and on them were the twelve names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.
καὶ τὸ τεῖχος τῆς πόλεως ἔχων θεμελίους δώδεκα, καὶ ἐπʼ αὐτῶν δώδεκα ὀνόματα τῶν δώδεκα ἀποστόλων τοῦ ἀρνίου.
The one who was speaking with me had a golden measuring reed to measure the city and its gates and its wall.[^22]
Καὶ ὁ λαλῶν μετʼ ἐμοῦ εἶχεν μέτρον κάλαμον χρυσοῦν, ἵνα μετρήσῃ τὴν πόλιν καὶ τοὺς πυλῶνας αὐτῆς καὶ τὸ τεῖχος αὐτῆς.
The city was laid out as a square; its length was the same as its width. He measured the city with the reed: 12,000 stadia.[^23] Its length and width and height are equal.
καὶ ἡ πόλις τετράγωνος κεῖται, καὶ τὸ μῆκος αὐτῆς ὅσον τὸ πλάτος. καὶ ἐμέτρησεν τὴν πόλιν τῷ καλάμῳ ἐπὶ σταδίους δώδεκα χιλιάδων· τὸ μῆκος καὶ τὸ πλάτος καὶ τὸ ὕψος αὐτῆς ἴσα ἐστίν.
He also measured its wall: 144 cubits[^24] by human measure, which is also an angel's measure.[^25]
καὶ ἐμέτρησεν τὸ τεῖχος αὐτῆς ἑκατὸν τεσσεράκοντα τεσσάρων πηχῶν, μέτρον ἀνθρώπου, ὅ ἐστιν ἀγγέλου.
The wall was built of jasper, and the city was pure gold, like clear glass.
καὶ ἡ ἐνδώμησις τοῦ τείχους αὐτῆς ἴασπις, καὶ ἡ πόλις χρυσίον καθαρὸν ὅμοιον ὑάλῳ καθαρῷ·
The foundations of the city wall were adorned with every kind of precious stone. The first foundation was jasper, the second sapphire, the third chalcedony, the fourth emerald,
οἱ θεμέλιοι τοῦ τείχους τῆς πόλεως παντὶ λίθῳ τιμίῳ κεκοσμημένοι· ὁ θεμέλιος ὁ πρῶτος ἴασπις, ὁ δεύτερος σάπφιρος, ὁ τρίτος χαλκηδών, ὁ τέταρτος σμάραγδος,
the fifth sardonyx, the sixth carnelian, the seventh chrysolite, the eighth beryl, the ninth topaz, the tenth chrysoprase, the eleventh jacinth and the twelfth amethyst.[^26]
ὁ πέμπτος σαρδόνυξ, ὁ ἕκτος σάρδιον, ὁ ἕβδομος χρυσόλιθος, ὁ ὄγδοος βήρυλλος, ὁ ἔνατος τοπάζιον, ὁ δέκατος χρυσόπρασος, ὁ ἑνδέκατος ὑάκινθος, ὁ δωδέκατος ἀμέθυστος·
The twelve gates were twelve pearls; each of the gates was made of a single pearl. And the street of the city was pure gold, like transparent glass.
καὶ οἱ δώδεκα πυλῶνες δώδεκα μαργαρῖται, ἀνὰ εἷς ἕκαστος τῶν πυλώνων ἦν ἐξ ἑνὸς μαργαρίτου· καὶ ἡ πλατεῖα τῆς πόλεως χρυσίον καθαρὸν ὡς ὕαλος διαυγής.
I saw no temple in the city, for its temple is the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb.
Καὶ ναὸν οὐκ εἶδον ἐν αὐτῇ, ὁ γὰρ κύριος, ὁ θεός, ὁ παντοκράτωρ, ναὸς αὐτῆς ἐστιν, καὶ τὸ ἀρνίον.
The city has no need of the sun or the moon to shine on it, for the glory of God gives it light, and its lamp is the Lamb.[^27]
καὶ ἡ πόλις οὐ χρείαν ἔχει τοῦ ἡλίου οὐδὲ τῆς σελήνης, ἵνα φαίνωσιν αὐτῇ, ἡ γὰρ δόξα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐφώτισεν αὐτήν, καὶ ὁ λύχνος αὐτῆς τὸ ἀρνίον.
The nations will walk by its light, and the kings of the earth bring their glory into it.[^28]
καὶ περιπατήσουσιν τὰ ἔθνη διὰ τοῦ φωτὸς αὐτῆς· καὶ οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς φέρουσιν τὴν δόξαν αὐτῶν εἰς αὐτήν·
Its gates will never be shut by day, for there will be no night there.[^29]
καὶ οἱ πυλῶνες αὐτῆς οὐ μὴ κλεισθῶσιν ἡμέρας, νὺξ γὰρ οὐκ ἔσται ἐκεῖ,
They will bring the glory and the honor of the nations into it.
καὶ οἴσουσιν τὴν δόξαν καὶ τὴν τιμὴν τῶν ἐθνῶν εἰς αὐτήν.
But nothing unclean will ever enter it,[^30] nor anyone who does what is detestable or false, but only those who are written in the Lamb's book of life.
καὶ οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθῃ εἰς αὐτὴν πᾶν κοινὸν καὶ ποιῶν βδέλυγμα καὶ ψεῦδος, εἰ μὴ οἱ γεγραμμένοι ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τῆς ζωῆς τοῦ ἀρνίου.
